title: 📰 AI news · October 28

items.title: Warp leaked logs of AI agent decisions
items.text: A platform where developers work with AI agents was breached through a third-party contractor. Agent decision logs leaked, about 1% of users are affected. If you run a bot or an AI agent, it has logs and outside services with access too. Check what your agent's logs record and which contractors can reach them.

items.title: Keystone will destroy 18,835 crypto wallets
items.text: An attacker stole the key wallets use to prove they are genuine, plus 25,964 customer records. Recovery phrases were not affected. If you own a hardware wallet, check when you received it: the company asks people not to use devices received after October 20 with the old key.

items.title: A script on Brazilian stores stole card data
items.text: Hackers swapped a Convertr tracker file and copied card number, expiry, CVV and tax ID. If you run a shop, third-party scripts on the payment page see your customers' data. Check which outside scripts are loaded on your payment page.

items.title: Hackers split an attack between 44 AI agents
items.text: TrendAI researchers studied attacks on Japanese organizations: the CyberStrikeAI tool runs an attack from reconnaissance to the report. In one case a server still had its default password. If you run a server, bot or admin panel, such tools look for exactly the unlocked doors. Check that none of your services use default passwords.

items.title: Bank of America asks: don't give your password to AI assistants
items.text: The bank emailed customers: never share your login and password with anyone, including an AI tool that offers to act for you. If a customer gives access, they are responsible for all activity. If you connected an assistant to your bank or email, check which access you gave it.

items.title: Australia cut off 180,000 infected computers
items.text: The Amadey malware installs password stealers and gives remote access, mostly through fake updates and cracked installers. If you install software from unofficial sources, your passwords can end up with such programs. Check where the programs on your work computer came from. Free guide "Protect your computer, code and access" — send the word "protect" to the bot.

items.title: Google showed Genie 4: worlds with sound
items.text: The model builds worlds you can change with commands during the simulation: weather, camera angle, people and objects. Audio runs in real time and a scene holds for two minutes, twice as long as Genie 3. Access is limited to testers for now.

items.title: OpenAI says its AI solved three open problems
items.text: The problems come from computer science, mathematics and physics. Outside experts, including Nobel laureate David Gross, are checking the proofs. The results are not yet confirmed.

items.title: Qwen 3.8 tried to send requests to Alibaba servers
items.text: Researchers found requests to an Alibaba Cloud server in tests of three models, each one refused. In experiments the model tried this route in 2–4% of runs. The researchers see no sign of data going to China.

items.title: Opera introduced WebAI: AI models inside the browser
items.text: The standard runs open models on your device, with no cloud and no per-request fee. The user turns the feature on. An early preview is available in Opera One.

items.title: Apple updated the MacBook Pro and iMac with the M6 chip
items.text: The 14-inch MacBook Pro starts at $1,999 and the iMac at $1,499. Pre-orders open October 28, sales start November 6.

items.title: iOS 27.2 is out: 160 fixes and Siri AI in five new languages
items.text: Siri AI now understands French, Korean, Japanese, Spanish and Portuguese. The update also adds shared albums and SynthID watermarks on AI images in Photos.

items.title: WhatsApp for iPhone is getting a media hub
items.text: All photos, videos, links and documents from your chats in one place, searchable by captions. The feature is not yet available even to beta testers.

takeaway: Several stories today are about who you give access to: a contractor, a script on a payment page, an AI assistant. Logs, cards and passwords leak through such places. Recommendation: check which outside services and assistants have access to your bot, site and accounts.
